div.head: II Cn 62
div.ab: Gif hwa hamsocne gewyrce, gebete þæt mid V pundan þam cingce on Engla lage (⁊ on Cent æt hamsocne V þam cingce ⁊ þreo þam arcebisceope), ⁊ Dena lage, swa hit ær stod.
Gif hwa hamsocne gewyrce, gebete þæt mid fif pundum þam cyninge on Engla lage, ⁊ on Dena lage, swa hit ær stod.
Si quis hamsocnam faciat, V libras emendet regi in Anglorum laga, et in Dena laga sicut lex stetit antea.
Hamsocne. Gyf hwa hamsocne gewyrce, gebete ðæt mid V pundum ðam kynincge on Engla lage, [⁊ on Dena] lage swa hit ær stod.

Attacks upon men's houses. If a man makes forcible entry into another man's house, he shall pay £5 to the king as compensation for so doing in districts under English law, and in the Danelaw the amount fixed by existing regulations.

(Heimsuchung. B) Wenn einer [widerrechtliche] Heimsuchung verübt, büsse er das mit 5 Pfund dem König in Engländer-Recht (und in Kent [gehören] von Heimsuchung[-Strafe] 5 [Pfund] dem König und 3 dem Erzbischof G), und im Dänen-Recht so, wie es bisher galt.

(Housebreaking. B) If anyone commits [unlawful] attack on a house, let him atone for it with 5 pounds to the king under English law (and in Kent, from the house-attack [penalty], 5 [pounds belong] to the king and 3 to the archbishop, G), and under Danish law as it has stood hitherto.
div.note: The words in brackets about Kent are only in G (a Kentish addition; Liebermann compares I Cn 3.2). G lacks ‘on’ before ‘Dena lage’; Liebermann supplies it from the other MSS. Only the italic formatting of K was corrected here.
